metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded at 250 Hz with a 74-channel Easycap passive Ag/AgCl cap, amplified by a MEGIN TRIUX system and referenced to the mastoids. Stimulus presentation and online feedback were run with BCI2000. Each trial had a 1 s inter-stimulus interval followed by a 5 s target presentation, with cursor feedback from 3 to 6 s. The protocol specified 32 trials per run.

citation_details.title: Neural mechanisms of training in Brain-Computer Interface : A Biophysical modeling approach
citation_details.author: A. Debnath, T. Venot, Marie-Constance Corsi, Parul Verma
citation_details.abstract: Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) is a system that translates neural activity into commands, allowing direct communication between brain and external devices. Despite its clinical application, BCIs are unable to robustly capture subjects’ intent due to limited understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying BCI control. To address this, we introduce a biophysical linear neural mass model to investigate the associated neural mechanisms of motor imagery BCI (MI-BCI) by modulating the scale-free spectral characteristics of afferent inputs. We tailor this motor imagery neural mass model (mi-NMM) to simulate both MI and resting-state activity and apply it to a cohort of 19 healthy subjects trained over four sessions, during which magnetoencephalography and electroencephalography signals were simultaneously recorded.
